title: Lesson 9: Fighting for Purity
description: Purity is not how you earn God's love. It is how you protect a heart that already belongs to Him. Through King David's fall, Jesus' words about the heart, and 1 Corinthians 6, you will learn what to do when temptation fires the starting gun: RUN. Remember the Cross, United with God, and Need others.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, the Closer to God Triangle showed that as two people draw near to God, they draw near to each other. Temptation pulls the opposite way, away from God and away from the people you love. This lesson is about purity, which means guarding your body, your eyes, and your mind, whether you are married or single. Like everything in the Christian life, it starts with grace.

blocks.alt: King David, fully clothed, alone on his palace roof overlooking the city, with his royal robe and crown set aside

blocks.title: The View from the Roof
blocks.text:
David was Israel's greatest king, a man the Bible describes as a man after God's own heart (1 Samuel 13:14). One spring, at the time when kings usually went out to battle, David stayed home in Jerusalem while his army went to war (2 Samuel 11:1).

Late one afternoon, he got up from his couch and walked on the roof of his palace. From there he saw a woman bathing. Instead of turning away, David pursued what he saw. He sent someone to find out who she was and learned that she was Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, one of his own soldiers. Then David used his power as king. He "sent messengers and took her" (2 Samuel 11:4).

When Bathsheba became pregnant, David tried to hide what he had done. When hiding failed, he arranged for Uriah to be killed in battle. One look became a string of choices, and each one made the next one easier. The chapter ends with one heavy sentence: "But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD" (2 Samuel 11:27).

David kept his sin hidden until God sent the prophet Nathan to confront him. Then David finally said, "I have sinned against the LORD." Nathan answered with words David did not deserve: "The LORD also has put away your sin" (2 Samuel 12:13).

David's story is a warning, but it is also a rescue. Years before, Joseph faced a similar temptation, and the Bible says "he left his garment in her hand and fled" (Genesis 39:12). Joseph ran, and David did not. Sin comes to steal, kill, and destroy, but Jesus came to give life.
The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I came that they may have life and have it abundantly.
Jesus did not just die to forgive your sin. He died to give you the power to fight it and to build your life on His direction instead of your desires.
9.1 - Consider David's story: a look, the wrong decision, hiding his sin, and a long silence. Why do you think the first steps matter so much when it comes to temptation?
The RUN Plan
Paul wrote to young Christians in Corinth, a city full of sexual temptation. Notice the words in bold. They are the RUN plan.

But he who is joined to the Lord becomes one spirit with him. Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body. Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body.

Flee means run. When temptation fires the starting gun, you have a split second to choose: run toward life, or stay and slide toward the pit. Do not see how close you can get. Close the app, turn off the show, or leave the room. Try it below.

R is for Remember the Cross. Temptation says your body is yours to use however you want. Paul says you are not your own, because you were bought with a price, and Jesus paid it at the cross. You are not fighting for purity so God will let you into His family. You are fighting because you are already in it, loved by a Father who paid everything to set you free.
9.2 - Has your fight for purity mostly been driven by fear of getting caught or by love for a Father who already calls you His own? What might change if love became the reason?

U is for United with God. This is the top of the Closer to God Triangle. You are joined to the Lord, and your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. You live to glorify God the Father, so you never run in your own strength. Run from sin and run to Jesus, who was "tempted as we are, yet without sin" (Hebrews 4:15). It can be as simple as whispering, "Lord Jesus, I need Your grace right now. Be my strength."
N is for Need others. Sin grows best in hiding, just as it did for David. Notice all the 2s in 2 Timothy 2:22, and let them remind you to run with at least two trusted believers.
So flee youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.

Not everything private is sinful, but a struggle you hide from everyone who could help you tends to grow in the dark. James says to "confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed" (James 5:16).
When the Thought Knocks
Purity starts in the heart. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said:
You have heard that it was said, 'You shall not commit adultery.' But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

A passing thought is not a sin, since Jesus Himself was tempted. A tempting thought is a knock at the door. Lust is opening the door and letting it stay (James 1:14-15). That is why Jesus told His followers to take drastic action against whatever leads them into sin (Matthew 5:29-30). Job decided ahead of time what he would do with his eyes:
I made a covenant with my eyes not to look lustfully at a young woman.

So when the thought knocks, run. Paul says to "take every thought captive to obey Christ" (2 Corinthians 10:5). Name the thought, hand it to Jesus, and choose what is good. Do not believe the lies temptation tells, like "No one will know" or "You're too far gone." Jesus called the devil a liar (John 8:44). Answer with the truth: Christ bought you at the cross, God lives in you, and you are not alone.
9.3 - What is one habit or boundary you can establish to better protect your mind and heart?
When You Have Already Fallen

Maybe you read David's story and thought, "That is me." The most important part of his story is what happened when he stopped hiding. God forgave him, and He will forgive you: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins" (1 John 1:9). Growth is often slow, and some struggles need time and wise help to heal, but God has not given up on you. "There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (Romans 8:1). Keep coming back to the Father, keep using the RUN plan, and let other believers walk with you.

blocks.title: If you have been harmed
content: If someone used their power to pressure or harm you sexually, what was done to you is not your sin to confess. It was sin against you. Please tell a pastor, a counselor, or another safe and trusted person, and let them help you get care.
If a child is being harmed, contact local authorities right away. If you are in immediate danger, call 911.

blocks.text: 9.4 - Who is one mature, trusted believer you could ask to pray for you and check in with you about purity? What would help you take that step? You do not need to write any private details here.
Lesson 9 Review

David did not run. His fall began with a look he pursued and grew in hiding, but his restoration began the moment he confessed. Purity is not how you earn God's love. It is how you protect a heart that already belongs to Him and the relationships inside the Closer to God Triangle. When temptation fires the starting gun, RUN: Remember the Cross, United with God, and Need others. In the next lesson, you will come to the table Jesus set for His people, where that same grace is put on display.
Closing Reflections
